Methods for fitted panel spatial probit models

Source: R/methods.R
psprobit-methods.Rd

Methods for fitted panel spatial probit models

Usage

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
summary(object, classification = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("prob", "link", "class"),
  draws = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
plot(x, pars = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
as_draws(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
tidy(x, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

x, object

A fitted psprobit object.

digits

Number of digits to print.

...

Unused.

classification

Logical; report in-sample classification statistics (see psp_classification()) in summary().

parm

Parameters for which intervals are returned (default: all).

level

Credible level.

newdata

Optional data frame for counterfactual predictions: the same units and periods as the fitted data, with new regressor values (the response column may be left out). Correlated-random-effects columns are kept at their fitted values, since they stand for fixed unit characteristics. Not available for models with lagged outcomes.

type

For predict(): "prob" (posterior mean probabilities; a matrix with one column per category for ordered models), "link" (posterior mean of the systematic part of the latent outcome) or "class" (most probable outcome).

draws

Number of posterior draws used by predict().

pars

Parameters to plot (default: all).

conf.level

Credible level for tidy().

Value

coef() a named vector, vcov() a matrix, confint() a matrix of interval bounds, summary() an object of class summary.psprobit, predict()/fitted() vectors or matrices in the row order of the data.
